hints.title: Divisibility Parity and Factor Rules
hints.text: A repunit number consists solely of the digit 1. Such numbers are always odd and never end in 0 or 5, so if k is divisible by 2 or 5, no valid solution exists.

hints.title: Iterative Remainder Progression
hints.text: Building repunits digit by digit corresponds to updating the remainder: rem = (rem * 10 + 1) % k. You only need to track the remainder, not the large integer itself.

hints.title: Pigeonhole Principle Termination
hints.text: There are only k possible remainders modulo k (0 to k - 1). By the Pigeonhole Principle, if 0 does not occur within k steps, a cycle has formed without reaching 0.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Constructing repunit strings or arbitrary-precision bigints wastes memory and causes numeric overflow.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Modular remainder simulation executes in at most k iterations using constant extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should quickly rule out multiples of 2 and 5 and apply the Pigeonhole Principle to bound the loop.
complexity.notes: Loop terminates in at most k steps.
